checks.do: Whether an alert is Resolved or Closed before trying to reopen it: only resolved alerts can be reopened.
Whether write access is enabled for the cloud account and the alert has Open status or remediation status Failure before remediating.

Whether an ignore filter applies to alerts that already exist: the Adding Alert Ignore Filters page says both that filters are applied only to newly triggered alerts and that all matching alerts are moved to ignored status.
Whether the alert rule is enabled, since ZPC sends alert notifications only when it is.

alert-types-severity.statement: ZPC alerts are Cloud Alerts (security policy violations in cloud resources at runtime) or IaC Alerts (misconfigurations in IaC infrastructure at build time), triaged by severity Critical, High, Low or Medium.

quotes: Cloud Alerts: Alerts triggered for security policy violations that occur within your cloud resources during runtime.
IaC Alerts: Alerts triggered for misconfigurations detected in your IaC infrastructure during build time.
ZPC triages the alerts by severity (Critical, High, Low, or Medium)

export-contributing-factors.statement: When the All Contributing Factors option is not selected in a Cloud Alerts export to Excel, only the first 15 aggregated findings are included.

quotes: All Contributing Factors: The aggregated findings of an alert that describes the security violation in the policy.
When this option is not selected, only the first 15 aggregated findings are included in the Export report.
On the Cloud Alerts tab, you can do the following:
Export the alert data along with the following attributes per your requirements to an Excel file and download the report:

notifications-tab.statement: The Notifications tab lists alert rules with Alert Type (Cloud or IaC), Integration Type (ServiceNow, Jira, Amazon Security Lake, AWS S3, Azure Blob, or Slack) and State; a rule added without configured notifications shows State Saved.

quotes: Alert Type: The type of alert (Cloud or IaC).
Integration Type: The third-party tool (ServiceNow, Jira, Amazon Security Lake, AWS S3, Azure Blob, or Slack) to which the alert notifications are sent.
When you initially add an alert rule but don't configure the notifications, the State is displayed as Saved.

ignore-filters-tab.statement: The Ignore Filters tab lists filters with Alert Type, Filter Scope, Created By, Updated By and an End Date, the date when the filter is going to be disabled.

quotes: Alert Type: The type of alert (cloud alert or IaC alert) that must be ignored.
Filter Scope: The list of entities on which the filter is applied.
End Date: The date when the filter is going to be disabled.
Created By: The admin who created the filter.
Updated By: The admin who updated the filter.

status-values.statement: ZPC alert statuses are Open, Closed, Resolved and Reopened; new alerts are Open, and ZPC grants Reopened automatically to a previously resolved alert.

quotes: Reopened | ZPC automatically grants this status to an existing alert that was previously resolved.
Alerts that are initially triggered are in Open status. When these alerts are evaluated and addressed, the status transitions to resolved or closed.
ZPC automatically grants this status to an existing alert that was previously resolved.

status-reopen-rule.statement: Only resolved alerts can be reopened; closed alerts cannot be reopened.

quotes: You can only reopen resolved alerts, but cannot reopen closed alerts.

status-closed-cloud.statement: Cloud alerts are Closed when they are no longer valid, for example when the cloud account is deleted or offboarded, the policy is deleted or deprecated, the custom policy query is edited, or the cloud resource is deleted.

quotes: Closed | Alerts that are no longer valid.

The cloud account is deleted or offboarded. The policy that the alert was triggered for is deleted. The predefined policy is deprecated as it is not relevant. The custom policy query is edited. The custom policy is deleted. The cloud resource is deleted.

status-closed-iac.statement: IaC alerts are Closed when the IaC Scan app or integration is deleted, the IaC subscription expires or is removed, the repository is permanently deleted or unsubscribed, or the resource or branch is deleted.

quotes: When the IaC Scan app or an IaC integration is deleted.
When the IaC subscription is expired or removed.
When the repository is permanently deleted or the repository is unsubscribed and is no longer being monitored by ZPC.
When the resource or branch is deleted.

attr-id-age-source.statement: The Alert Age attribute is the number of days an alert was in Open status, and the Alert Source is ZPC so third-party systems can identify the product that generated the alert.

quotes: | Alert Age | The number of days an alert was in Open status | 10 days |
| Alert Source | The source is ZPC. This data helps third-party systems to identify the security product that generated the alert. |  |

attr-status-description.statement: Alert Status Description describes the transition of an alert from one status to another, with sample values Auto Resolved and Manually Deleted.

quotes: | Alert Status Description | Describes the transition of the alert from one status to another. | Auto Resolved Manually Deleted |

attr-remediation.statement: The remediation attributes are Supports Remediation, Remediation Allowed, Remediation Initiated By (Zscaler if remediated automatically through alert management flow) and Remediation Status, with sample values Progress, Success, Failed and Blank.

quotes: | Supports Remediation | Indicates that remediation can be enabled for a policy | True False |
| Remediation Initiated By | The admin who initiated the remediation action | Zscaler (if the alert was remediated automatically through alert management flow) |
| Remediation Status | The status of the remediation | Progress Success Failed Blank |
| Remediation Allowed | Indicates whether remediation is allowed for a policy. This is applicable when remediation is enabled for a policy. | True False |

attr-trusted-ip.statement: The Trusted IP attribute is True when the alert is publicly exposed and associated with a trusted IP list, False when publicly exposed but not associated, and - when not publicly exposed and not associated.

quotes: True: The alert is publicly exposed and associated with a trusted IP list. False: The alert is publicly exposed but not associated with a trusted IP list. -: The alert is not publicly exposed and not associated with a trusted IP list.

attr-identity-power.statement: Identity Power Category applies only to identities with a power score of more than 80, and Identity Power Score is a numeric score (sample 1-100) based on an internal Zscaler IP calculation of power.

quotes: | Identity Power Category | Applicable only to identities with a power score of more than 80. | Data Compute Billing |
| Identity Power Score | The numeric score granted to an identity based on an internal Zscaler IP calculation of power. | 1–100 |

attr-azure-resource-id.statement: Azure Resource IDs are displayed in lowercase in the Resource ID attribute, regardless of the case in which they were created.

quotes: Azure Resource IDs are displayed in lowercase, regardless of the case in which they are originally created.

attr-iac-fields.statement: IaC alert attributes include Template Type (sample Terraform, CFT, ARM, Kubernetes YAML, Helm charts), Scan Plugin (sample GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Azure Pipelines, GitHub Actions, Azure Repos, Terraform Cloud) and Scan Type (sample Push, Pull, Build); Branch is not applicable for CI/CD integration.

quotes: | Template Type | The type of IaC template | Terraform CFT ARM Kubernetes YAML Helm charts |
| Scan Plugin | The type of IaC plugin | GitHub GitLab Jenkins Azure Pipelines GitHub Actions Azure Repos Jenkins Terraform Cloud |
| Scan Type | The activity that triggered the scan | Push Pull Build |
This is not applicable for CI/CD integration.

attr-policy.statement: The Policy Source attribute is Predefined or custom (sample Zscaler or Custom), and Theme is the security policy theme (sample Compliance, Security Exposure, Security Events or blank).

quotes: | Policy Source | Predefined or custom security policy | Zscaler Custom |
| Theme | The security policy theme | Compliance Security Exposure Security Events Blank (-) |

threat-categories.statement: ZPC assigns each policy violation a threat category and severity; the categories include Account Takeover, Authentication Misconfiguration, Crypto mining, Dormant Accounts, External Exposure, Multilayer Attack Paths, Permission Misconfiguration, Privilege Escalation, Ransomware, Reconnaissance and Evasion, Security Events and Attack Vector, Security Exposure, Service Misconfiguration, Stale Data and Assets, and Suspicious Activity.

quotes: The policy violations are assigned a specific threat category and a severity level
| Account Takeover | Suspicious and unusual activity patterns that do not resemble normal activity and suggest an account takeover |
| Authentication Misconfiguration | Bad practice or misconfiguration of authentication settings that lead to easy access of important resources resulting in high security risk |
| Crypto mining | Setup and activities suspected to be related to crypto mining |
| Dormant Accounts | User accounts that are not used over a long period of time |
| External Exposure | Publicly exposed resources |
| Multilayer Attack Paths | Correlated activities and settings that compose a complete attack vector into your system |
| Permission Misconfiguration | Bad practice or risky permission settings |

| Privilege Escalation | Configuration issues that directly or indirectly allow for privilege escalation (e.g., users with basic permissions implement various techniques to gain administrator privileges) |
| Reconnaissance and Evasion | Activities and configuration changes that often occur during reconnaissance and evasion attempts during an attack |
| Security Events and Attack Vector | Alerts related to security events such as suspicious user activity, and advanced attack vectors that allow for high-risk exploitation of the system |
| Security Exposure | Alerts related to security exposure, such as bad configurations, permissions, etc. |
| Service Misconfiguration | Services that are badly configured leading to advanced attacks |
| Ransomware | Improper configurations and suspicious activities that indicate a potential ransomware attack. |
| Stale Data and Assets | Images and data that are stored for a very long time with no changes |
| Suspicious Activity | Tracking uncommon risky activities that may indicate an attack |

drawer-timeline.statement: In the Cloud Alert drawer, Timeline alert data is captured every 5 minutes and alert history is by default shown for the last month; some repository details are not displayed for Jenkins Pipeline scans in the IaC Alert drawer.

quotes: The alert data is captured every 5 minutes. By default, the alert history is displayed for the last month.
Some repository details are not displayed for Jenkins Pipeline scans due to a limitation in processing.
The Cloud Alert drawer has the following tabs:
- Timeline: View the history of the alert that includes the following details:
The IaC Alert drawer has the following tabs:

rule-enable-required.statement: ZPC sends alert notifications only when the alert rule is enabled, and a rule can be configured first and enabled later.

quotes: ZPC sends alert notifications only when you've enabled the alert rule.
You can initially configure the alert rule and notification, but enable the notification at a later point in time.

rule-prereq-channels.statement: An alert rule needs onboarded cloud accounts or a completed IaC integration; ZPC sends email notifications to recipients and can send alert notifications and data to ITSM, cloud storage and ChatOps tools.

quotes: You must first onboard your cloud accounts or complete the IaC integration before adding cloud or IaC alert rules.
ZPC triggers alerts in the event of any security policy violations and sends email notifications to recipients to take the necessary action.
You can integrate ZPC with third-party tools (ITSM, cloud storage services, and ChatOps), and send alert notifications and alert data to these tools for incident management.

rule-scope-cloud.statement: A cloud alert rule scope can be set by Business Units, Clouds (AWS, Azure or GCP), Accounts, Regions and Select Policy, with policies filterable by Compliance, Severity, Threat Category or Policy Type.

quotes: - Business Units: Select the business units that must be associated with this alert rule.
- Clouds: Select the cloud service provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
- Select Policy: Select the security policies that must be included in this the alert rule. Use the Compliance, Severity, Threat Category, or Policy Type filter to search for policies.
- Accounts: Select the cloud accounts that must be included in this alert rule.
- Regions: Select the regions that must be included in this alert rule.

rule-scope-iac.statement: An IaC alert rule scope can be set by Scan Plugin, Repository and Select Policy, with policies filterable by Compliance, Severity or Policy Type.

quotes: - Scan Plugin: Select the IaC plugins for which alert notifications must be sent.
- Repository: Select the IaC repositories for which the alert notifications must be sent.
- Select Policy: Select the security policies for which the alert notifications must be sent. Use the Compliance, Severity, or Policy Type filter to search for specific policies.

rule-email-options.statement: The email notification of an alert rule has a Frequency of Daily or Weekly, a Send At time, a Timezone, an optional detailed report attachment and recipient addresses.

quotes: - Frequency: Select the frequency (Daily or Weekly) of the notification.
- Send At: Select the time when the email must be sent to the recipient.
- Include detailed report: Select the checkbox to send the alert report as an email attachment.
- Timezone: Select the time zone for the notification.
- Recipients: Enter the email addresses of recipients.

rule-status-email-each-time.statement: In the Alert Rule Status step, the page says email notifications are sent every time the alert is triggered.

quotes: Alert Rule Status: Click the toggle to enable the status. Email notifications are sent every time the alert is triggered.

rule-itsm-options.statement: An ITSM notification in an alert rule selects ServiceNow or JIRA, an alert payload of Audit Procedure, Remediation and Resource Metadata, an assignee email, and checkboxes to send notifications for closed and resolved alerts.

quotes: - Select ServiceNow or JIRA.
- Include in alert payload: Select the data that must be included in the alert payload.
- Send notifications for closed alerts: Select the checkbox to send notifications for closed alerts.
- Send notifications for resolved alerts: Select the checkbox to send notifications for resolved alerts.
- Audit Procedure: Steps to audit the policy violation.
- Remediation: Steps to remediate the policy violation.
- Resource Metadata: The metadata of the asset or identity.
- Assignee: Enter the recipient's email ID.
evidence.after: - Recipients: Enter the email addresses of recipients.

rule-slack-option.statement: An alert rule's Slack notification selects Slack and then the channels to which the alert notifications must be sent.

quotes: Select Slack, then select the required channels to which the alert notifications must be sent.

ignore-filter-newly-triggered.statement: Ignore filters are applied only to newly triggered alerts.

quotes: The ignore filters are applied only to the newly triggered alerts.

ignore-filter-created-moves.statement: The page says all alerts matching the selected criteria are moved to ignored status.

quotes: All the alerts matching the selected criteria are moved to ignored status.

ignore-filter-permission.statement: By default only users with the admin and security operations (SecOps) role can add ignore filters; other ZPC users have view-only permission unless Ignore Rules permissions are added or modified in Global Modules.

quotes: By default, users with admin and security operations (SecOps) role can add ignore filters. All other ZPC users have view-only permission.
You can enable the add permission to other ZPC users by adding or modifying Ignore Rules permissions in Global Modules.

ignore-filter-end-date.statement: An ignore filter is disabled after its end date, after which alerts are triggered for security policy violations.

quotes: This filter is disabled after the end date and alerts are triggered for security policy violations.

ignore-filter-scope-cloud.statement: A cloud ignore filter needs at least one of Policies, Cloud Accounts, Cluster Names, Namespaces, Tags or Assets; Next is disabled if none is selected.

quotes: - For Cloud Alerts, select at least one of the filters below:
- Cluster Names
- Namespaces
- If no filters are selected within the scope, the Next button is disabled.
- Policies
- Cloud Accounts
- Assets
Click the Tags drop-drown menu and choose Select Tags.

ignore-filter-scope-iac.statement: An IaC ignore filter needs at least one of Policies, Template Type, Scan Plugin or Repository, and Template Type options are Terraform, CloudFormation, Azure Resource Manager, Kubernetes, Helm Charts and Terraform Plan.

quotes: - For IaC Alerts, select at least one of the filters below:
- Template Type
Select one or more template type (Terraform, CloudFormation, Azure Resource Manager, Kubernetes, Helm Charts, Terraform Plan) from the drop-down menu.
- Policies
- Scan Plugin
- Repository
evidence.after: - If no filters are selected within the scope, the Next button is disabled.

ignore-filter-defaults.statement: In a cloud ignore filter the All Policies, All Accounts, All Kubernetes Clusters, All Kubernetes Namespaces, All Tags and All Assets options are selected by default.

quotes: By default, the All Policies filter is selected.
By default, the All Accounts filter is selected.
By default, the All Kubernetes Clusters filter is selected.
By default, the All Kubernetes Namespaces filter is selected.
By default, the All Tags filter is selected.
By default, the All Assets filter is selected.
evidence.after: - Policy Focus: Select Asset or Identity from the Policy Focus drop-down menu.

ignore-filter-delete.statement: A deleted ignore filter is not applicable to newly triggered alerts, and alerts already ignored under it remain ignored.

quotes: The deleted filter is not applicable to any newly triggered alert. Existing ignored alerts under this filter will remain ignored even after deleting the filter.

ignore-alert-behavior.statement: When an alert is ignored, ZPC still triggers the alert whenever it detects the policy violation, but the alert notification is not sent to third-party tools; ignoring requires a reason and a duration.

quotes: In the Ignore Alert window, enter the reason and select the duration for ignoring the alert.
However, the alert notification is not sent to third-party tools.
The alert is ignored, but whenever ZPC detects a security policy violation, it triggers the alert.

resolve-alert.statement: Resolving an alert requires a reason and changes the alert status to Resolved.

quotes: In the Resolve Alert window, enter the reason for resolving the alert.
The alerts are resolved and the alert status changes to Resolved on the Alerts page.

remediate-prereq.statement: Cloud alerts can be remediated manually only if write access is enabled for the cloud account, and only alerts with Open status or with remediation status Failure can be remediated.

quotes: Ensure that write access is enabled for the cloud account to allow remediation.
You can only remediate alerts with an Open status or alerts whose remediation status is Failure.
You can manually remediate cloud alerts triggered for policy violations.

remediate-scope.statement: Cloud alerts can be remediated singly, in multiples, in bulk or all alerts for a specific policy violation, using Remediate All on the Alerts Grouped By Policy tab, with a reason entered.

quotes: You can remediate single alert, multiple alerts, bulk alerts, or all alerts triggered for a specific policy violation.
4. Click the Actions icon () and select Remediate All.
5. In the Remediate Alerts window, enter the reason for remediation.

rule-email-timing.summary: The Adding Alert Rules page says email notifications are sent every time the alert is triggered and also offers a Daily or Weekly email Frequency.

positions.says: Email notifications are sent every time the alert is triggered.

quotes: Alert Rule Status: Click the toggle to enable the status. Email notifications are sent every time the alert is triggered.

positions.says: The email notification has a Frequency of Daily or Weekly.

quotes: - Frequency: Select the frequency (Daily or Weekly) of the notification.

rule-email-timing.impact: Whether an email goes out per trigger or on the Daily or Weekly schedule is not settled by the page.

ignore-filter-existing-alerts.summary: The Adding Alert Ignore Filters page says ignore filters apply only to newly triggered alerts and also that all alerts matching the selected criteria are moved to ignored status.

positions.says: Ignore filters are applied only to newly triggered alerts.

quotes: The ignore filters are applied only to the newly triggered alerts.

positions.says: All alerts matching the selected criteria are moved to ignored status.

quotes: All the alerts matching the selected criteria are moved to ignored status.

ignore-filter-existing-alerts.impact: Whether alerts that already exist are ignored when a filter is created is not settled by the page.

remediate-non-aws.title: Whether Azure and GCP cloud alerts can be remediated manually
remediate-non-aws.detail: The Remediating Alerts page says cloud alerts can be remediated and links write access only to Configuring Write Access for an AWS Cloud Account; the July 12, 2023 release note (zpc.release-notes#manual-remediation-2023-07) says 'AWS alerts'. No captured page states Azure or GCP remediation. The claims state what the page says about cloud alerts.

misconfiguration-category.title: Whether Misconfiguration is a threat category
misconfiguration-category.detail: The Alert Attributes sample for Threat Category lists Misconfiguration, which is not in the Threat Categories table (Authentication, Permission and Service Misconfiguration are).

alert-status-sample.title: Whether the Alert Status attribute sample is the full list
alert-status-sample.detail: The Alert Attributes sample lists Open, Closed and Resolved, while the Alert Status page lists four statuses including Reopened. The claims state what each page says.

remediation-failed-name.title: Whether the failed remediation status is named Failure or Failed
remediation-failed-name.detail: The Remediating Alerts page says remediation status Failure and the Alert Attributes sample lists Failed. The claims state what each page says.

cloud-rule-tags-scope.title: Whether Tags are an alert rule scope option for cloud alert rules
cloud-rule-tags-scope.detail: The Adding Alert Rules page lists Business Units, Clouds, Accounts, Regions and Select Policy, while the Amazon Security Lake page lists Tags as well. The claims state what each page says.

alert-limits.title: Limits on alert rules and ignore filters
alert-limits.detail: The number of alert rules or ignore filters per tenant and the maximum ignore duration are not stated in the captured pages.
